_meta.indication: LUMISIGHT is indicated for fluorescence imaging in adults with breast cancer as an adjunct for the intraoperative detection of cancerous tissue within the resection cavity following removal of the primary specimen during lumpectomy surgery.

pivotal_trials.phase: Pivotal (adequate and well-controlled) trial; primary evidence of effectiveness
pivotal_trials.design: Prospective, multicenter, 2-arm, randomized, intra-patient control study; patients randomized 10:1 between device arm and control arm, all clinical staff blinded to arm.
pivotal_trials.population: Adults with breast cancer undergoing breast conserving surgery (lumpectomy); patients received 1 mg/kg LUMISIGHT IV 2 to 6 hours prior to surgery.
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Three co-primary endpoints: patient-level removal of residual cancer (threshold 3%), tissue-level sensitivity (threshold 40%), and tissue-level specificity (threshold 60%); for study success all three co-primary endpoints were to exceed their prespecified success thresholds. CL0007 did not meet the predefined success criteria because tissue-level sensitivity did not exceed the 40% threshold.
pivotal_trials.n: N=406 received LUMISIGHT (safety population); 357 randomized to the device (imaging) arm (mITT population) and 35 to the control arm, with 14 withdrawals.
pivotal_trials.result: Patient-level removal of residual cancer was 27 of 357 patients (7.6%; 95% CI 5.0%, 10.8%), exceeding the 3% goal. Tissue-level specificity was 87% (95% CI 85%, 88%), exceeding the 60% goal. Tissue-level sensitivity was 49% (34/69; 95% CI 36%, 62%), which did not meet its 40% performance goal lower-bound.

key_safety: Adverse reactions occurring in ≥1% were hypersensitivity (1.4%, including anaphylaxis in 4 of 726) and chromaturia (85%); chromaturia resolved within 48 hours in 93% of patients (longest 15 days). Anaphylaxis occurred in 4/726 (0.6%) of patients.
target_moa: Pegulicianine is an optically inactive prodrug containing a Cy5 fluorophore and a QSY21 quencher connected by a peptide backbone; it produces a near-infrared fluorescent signal after the peptide backbone is cleaved by proteases (including cathepsins and matrix metalloproteases) that have higher activity in and around tumor tissue than normal cells.
modality: Optical imaging agent — an optical imaging drug constituent of a combination product (LUMISIGHT for injection plus the Lumicell DVS device constituent); a peptide-based fluorescent imaging prodrug.

boxed_warning.content: Boxed warning for anaphylaxis and other serious hypersensitivity reactions, which can occur during or following administration; anaphylaxis occurred in 4/726 (0.6%) of patients in clinical studies.

rems.type: No REMS was implemented; most Advisory Committee members did not support a REMS, considering it unnecessary for this drug.

advisory_committee.vote: The Medical Imaging Drugs Advisory Committee met March 5, 2024; on whether the benefits of pegulicianine outweigh its risks the vote was Yes: 16, No: 2, Abstain: 1.

basis.text: The 505(b)(1) NDA 214511 was designated Priority review.

summary.text: LUMISIGHT (pegulicianine) was approved as a 505(b)(1) NDA under Priority review as a new molecular entity, supported by one adequate and well-controlled trial (CL0007) with confirmatory evidence from CL0006, following a favorable Medical Imaging Drugs Advisory Committee vote. FDA required a post-marketing observational study (PMR 4614-1) to evaluate and characterize anaphylactic and other serious hypersensitivity reactions.

citations.quote: This 505(b)(1) NDA submission contains data from the pivotal clinical study (Study CL0007) and the clinical feasibility study (Study CL0006) of LUMISIGHT, an investigational new molecular entity optical imaging drug to detect cancerous tissue remaining in the lumpectomy cavity after excising the primary specimen during BCS.

After considering the above issues, we find that the Applicant has submitted substantial evidence of effectiveness for LUMISIGHT as an adjunct to detect breast cancer within the resection cavity after completion of BCS. This evidence is composed of one adequate and well-controlled study (CL0007) and confirmatory evidence of effectiveness provided in CL0006.
4614-1 Conduct a prospective observational study of sufficient sample size to evaluate the incidence of and characterize anaphylactic reactions to Lumisight in adults with breast cancer.

requirement.text: 4614-1 Conduct a prospective observational study of sufficient sample size to evaluate the incidence of and characterize anaphylactic reactions to Lumisight in adults with breast cancer. A secondary study objective will be to evaluate the incidence of and characterize other serious hypersensitivity reactions.

citations.quote: 4614-1 Conduct a prospective observational study of sufficient sample size to evaluate the incidence of and characterize anaphylactic reactions to Lumisight in adults with breast cancer. A secondary study objective will be to evaluate the incidence of and characterize other serious hypersensitivity reactions. Adverse events of interest should be pre-defined. Study assessments should include assessment of adverse events of interest (including laboratory data as needed), physical examination, and assessment of blood pressure, heart rate, and oxygen saturation before and at multiple timepoints after Lumisight administration. Adjudicate (using an external expert panel) suspected cases of anaphylaxis and serious hypersensitivity reactions.
